chunks: From him, from Abu Ja'far, from his father, from Ahmad ibn al-Nadhr, from 'Amr ibn Shimir, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
"If a man has a slave whom he employs, and the slave is agreeable to him, and he is kind to him, he should not sell him, and there is no reward for him."

key_terms.وَلَا كَرَامَةَ لَهُ: And there is no reward (for him if he sells him)
key_terms.يَسْتَتْبِعُهُ: He employs him / makes him work for him

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on selling a slave who is agreeable and kind to his master?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this hadith from Imam al-Baqir (AS) establishes a specific legal nuance where a master is advised against selling a slave who is both agreeable and kind, thereby preserving the bond for eventual emancipation. This ruling highlights the Shia emphasis on *ihsan* (excellence in conduct) as a catalyst for social liberation, distinguishing between mere ownership and the moral duty to nurture a slave's potential for freedom.
